---
title: SearcherKit Architecture
---

SearcherKit separates model communication, agent reasoning, retrieval, tool
presentation, and batch execution. This separation is the central design idea
behind both the code and its configuration.

## Execution flow

```text
dataset or TUI
      |
      v
 AgentRunner ---- checkpoint, logs, per-task retry
      |
      v
 SearchAgent ---- turn, token, and time budgets
      |
      +---- Parser <----> LLM Client <----> model endpoint
      |
      +---- Tool ----> Source ----> file, web, or Elasticsearch
      |
      `---- Tool ----> MCP server
```

`AgentRunner` owns workload concerns such as concurrency, checkpointing, output
files, and whole-task retries. `SearchAgent` owns one trajectory: it formats the
conversation, calls the model, dispatches tools, and asks for a final answer as
configured limits approach.

## Core concepts

### LLM client and parser

The client performs provider or inference-server I/O. The parser translates
between SearcherKit messages and a model's chat or tool-call format. Keeping
them separate lets an OpenAI-compatible endpoint serve models with different
prompt and tool-call conventions.

Use the `upstream` parser when the provider returns native tool calls. Use a
model-specific parser when tool calls are encoded in model text.

### Source and tool

A source retrieves documents. A tool is the model-visible action that uses a
source or another service. Multiple tools can share a source, and a tool can
present a deliberately small JSON Schema even when its implementation accepts
more parameters.

Built-in source families are local files, web search and fetch, and
Elasticsearch. Built-in tool families include search, visit, multi-source
variants, summarization, and MCP-backed tools.

### Config and factories

Runtime objects support structured configuration as well as normal Python
construction. Hydra composes YAML for CLI workflows; factory functions convert
the resulting config into clients, parsers, sources, and tools. Custom modules
are referenced by their real import paths rather than compatibility aliases.

### Outputs and traces

Batch execution writes one durable history record per sample, trace logs for
individual trajectories, a global run log, and aggregate summary data. These
artifacts are the handoff between running, evaluation, debugging, conversion,
and training workflows.

### Training integrations

Training reuses the same agent, parser, tools, sources, and trajectory format as
normal inference. `searcherkit.training` adapts those runtime components to a
training framework.

```text
AReaL or Slime
      |
      v
 Rollout worker ---- submit task, provide LLM endpoint, collect token sequence.
      |
      v
 SearchAgent ---- turn, token, and time budgets
      |
      ...
```

The supervised fine-tuning path converts saved trajectories into the target
dataset format and launches training from structured persistant config. 

The reinforcement-learning integrations run `SearchAgent` inside framework-owned
rollout workers, preserving conversation and tool behavior while translating
framework requests, responses, rewards, and trajectory metadata at the
integration boundary.

Framework-specific adapters live under `searcherkit.training.areal` and
`searcherkit.training.slime`; reusable training-agent and reward logic stays in
`searcherkit.training`. Shell launchers and cluster-specific defaults live in
`scripts/`. See the [training overview](../02-training/01-training-overview.qmd),
[SFT guide](../02-training/04-sft.qmd), [AReaL guide](../02-training/02-rl-areal.qmd),
and [slime guide](../02-training/03-rl-slime.qmd) for configuration and launch
details.

## Ownership map

| Concern | Owning package |
| --- | --- |
| Reasoning loop and final-answer control | `searcherkit.agent` |
| Provider API transport | `searcherkit.llm` |
| Model message and tool-call formats | `searcherkit.llm.parsers` |
| Search backend adapters | `searcherkit.sources` |
| Model-callable actions | `searcherkit.tools` |
| Batch, checkpoints, traces, evaluation | `searcherkit.runtime` |
| Config composition and user commands | `searcherkit.cli` |
| Dataset conversion and index deployment | `searcherkit.plugins` |
| SFT and RL integrations | `searcherkit.training` and `scripts/` |

This ownership map should also guide documentation changes: explain a concept
once in the guide, keep command syntax in the CLI reference, and keep exact
Python signatures in the generated API Reference.
